title: Counterexamples to the Mathieu Property: From Explicit Quotient Constructions to a General Classification
description: We construct regular functions $P,Q$ on each of $\SL_2/2O$ and $\SL_2/2I$ for which every positive Haar moment of $P$ vanishes, whereas $\h(QP^m)$ is nonzero for infinitely many $m$. The same elementary construction also supplies a radial witness on the defining module of $\SU(2)$. These three examples give the following classification: for a complex homogeneous space $G/H$, with $G$ and $H$ having reductive identity components, the kernel of normalized Reynolds integration is Mathieu--Zhao exactly when $[G^0,G^0]\subseteq H$. We give the reduction to the examples, including disconnected acting groups. The counterexamples are proved directly from Haar integration, polynomial identities and Dirichlet's theorem. For either exceptional example and each positive degree, one explicit fixed multiplier, chosen independently of the complex coefficients, gives a transcendental ordinary Cauchy transform for every polynomial recomposition of that degree. Over an arbitrary coefficient algebra, we also determine the pure and safe elements of the polynomial subalgebra generated by the example.
